notable_absence.finding: Revision pruning is described as automatic ('It automatically runs whenever a new revision is generated') with no manual trigger and no ordering precondition relative to any other operation - unlike resync.md's ordering dependency on database-offline, pruning has no documented sequencing requirement at all.

cross_component_finding: The revision cache (sgw:revision-cache) and channel cache (sgw:channel-cache, minted in managing-tombstones.json) are two separate in-memory caches this batch had to distinguish carefully - both are tuned via similar-shaped settings (a size limit and a memory limit) and both interact with tombstones (chan_cache_tombstone_revs vs rev cache eviction), but this page and managing-tombstones.md never state a relationship between the two caches themselves, only that both are affected by tombstone volume. Kept separate.
cross_product_finding: The Hybrid Logical Vector / HLV implementation this page describes for Sync Gateway 4.0+ is explicitly stated to be shared machinery with Couchbase Server's own XDCR cross-cluster versioning: 'Sync Gateway uses the Hybrid Logical Vector implementation described in HLV Data Maintained in xattr ... for XDCR compatibility.' This is a genuine cross-product mechanism-sharing statement (not a same-shape-different-product near-miss like sgcollect_info/cbcollect_info) - the SAME versioning mechanism spans both products by design, evidenced directly on the page rather than inferred. Reconciliation formalized this as sgw:version-vector -reliesOnMechanism-> xdcr:cross-cluster-versioning (see relations above).
